journeyTemplate.name: Emergency Fund Setup
journeyTemplate.purpose: New user → personalised EF target with attribution → 3-layer liquidity allocation → monthly contribution plan with milestones. The 8 sizing dimensions seed the user profile for all future features.
journeyTemplate.advisoryConstraint: Recommend instrument TYPES (savings account, liquid fund, short-term FD) — NEVER name specific banks, funds, or products.

formulaRecipe.overview:
The Emergency Fund Target (EFT) in INR: EFT = max(0, (B × H_target) + Ω − L)
B = Crisis-Mode Burn Rate (monthly) H_target = Recommended Time Horizon (months) Ω = Absolute Contingency Add-ons (one-time lump sum) L = Liquidity Offset (existing earmarked liquid savings)

variable.name: B
variable.label: Crisis-Mode Burn Rate
variable.definition: The minimum monthly family spend if income stopped tomorrow. This is essential survival cost — NOT standard monthly expenses.
variable.composition:
B = essential monthly expenses (non-discretionary household spend, EXCLUDING housing and EMIs) + housing costs (rent or owned-home maintenance) + secured debt obligations (home loan EMI, car loan EMI — obligations that cannot be paused)
EXCLUDES: - SIP/investment commitments (would be paused in crisis) - Discretionary spending (entertainment, dining out, shopping) - Insurance premiums (included in fixed obligations for H calculation, but not in crisis burn rate)
variable.toolCall: sum([essential monthly expenses, housing costs, secured debt obligations])

variable.name: H_target
variable.label: Recommended Time Horizon
variable.definition: Total runway needed in months. Computed from a base horizon adjusted by a cumulative risk multiplier, clamped to [3, 24].
variable.composition:
H_target = max(3, min(24, H_base × (1 + M_risk)))
H_base: Determined by employment type. Pick value from mappingTable "h_base_by_employment". M_risk: Cumulative risk adjustment. Sum of individual adjustments picked from risk_adj_by_age, risk_adj_by_income_sources, risk_adj_by_dependency, risk_adj_by_insurance, risk_adj_by_health mapping tables.
variable.toolCall: Step 1: H_base = pick value from h_base_by_employment for user's employmentType Step 2: M_risk = sum of all risk adjustments picked from mapping tables Step 3: H_raw = multiply(H_base, sum([1, M_risk])) Step 4: H_target = max(3, min(24, H_raw))

variable.name: H_ui_bands
variable.label: 3-Band UI Display
variable.composition: H_ui_min (Minimum Safe) = H_target × 0.75 H_ui_max (Strong Buffer) = H_target × 1.25 These are for UI display only — the recommended target is H_target.

variable.name: Ω
variable.label: Absolute Contingency Add-ons
variable.definition: One-time lump sum buffers for known shortfalls that cannot be absorbed by the monthly horizon.
variable.composition:
Ω = medical_buffer + contextual_buffer
medical_buffer: Triggered when user has NO health insurance. Pick value from mappingTable "medical_buffer_no_insurance" using cityTier. If user HAS adequate health insurance (≥₹10L cover), medical_buffer = 0.
contextual_buffer: From D9 (open/contextual factors user volunteers). Converted to a one-time INR amount by Pro's judgment. Bounded by [0.5 × B, 2 × B] when B is already computed. If B is not yet available, use [₹10,000, ₹2,00,000] as absolute INR bounds.

variable.name: L
variable.label: Liquidity Offset
variable.definition: Earmarked liquid assets the user already has set aside for emergencies.
variable.composition:
L = existing earmarked liquid savings (from profile)
This is the amount the user has ALREADY earmarked for emergencies — not total savings, not investment portfolio.
variable.toolCall: Direct read from profile. No computation needed.

formulaRecipe.starterShield: DETERMINISTIC RULE (not Pro judgment): If EFT ≤ existing savings (L ≥ EFT), user already has a sufficient fund. Transition to health-check framing instead of build-from-scratch.
formulaRecipe.liquidityAllocation:
After EFT is computed, allocate across three layers: Layer 1 (Instant Access): 1-2 months of B → savings account / sweep-in FD Layer 2 (Quick Access): 2-4 months of B → liquid mutual fund Layer 3 (Stable Reserve): remaining months → short-term FD / ultra-short debt fund
Adaptive rule: Freelancers/gig workers → weight toward Layer 1 (income is lumpy). Dual-income salaried → weight toward Layer 2/3 (natural income hedge).

table.name: h_base_by_employment
table.description: Base time horizon before risk adjustments. Higher = more months needed.

table.name: risk_adj_by_age
table.description: Risk multiplier adjustment based on career stage. Added to other risk adjustments.

table.name: risk_adj_by_income_sources
table.description: Risk multiplier adjustment based on household income diversity.

entry.note: Some hedge but one variable income
Single point of failure but stable

table.name: dep_adj_spouse
table.description: Adjustment for non-working spouse. Direct lookup from spouseEmploymentStatus.

table.name: dep_adj_children_under5
table.description: Adjustment for children under 5. Pre-computed total by count (capped at 0.15). For count > 2, use defaultAbove key.

table.name: dep_adj_children_school
table.description: Adjustment for school-age children. Pre-computed total by count (capped at 0.20). School fees are fixed obligations. For count > 2, use defaultAbove key.

table.name: dep_adj_aging_parent_insured
table.description: Adjustment for insured aging parents. 0.05 per parent. For count > 2, use defaultAbove key.

table.name: dep_adj_aging_parent_uninsured
table.description: Adjustment for uninsured aging parents. 0.15 per parent — significant medical risk. For count > 2, use defaultAbove key.

table.name: dep_adj_other
table.description: Adjustment for other dependents (sibling, relative, etc.). 0.05 per dependent. For count > 2, use defaultAbove key.

table.name: risk_adj_by_insurance
table.description: Risk multiplier for insurance coverage quality. Use classificationLogic to derive key, then pick entry value.
table.classificationLogic: Read three profile fields: healthInsuranceCoverAmount, termLifeCoverAmount, healthInsuranceSource. Apply rules in priority order (first matching rule wins): Rule 1: healthInsuranceCoverAmount >= 1000000 AND termLifeCoverAmount > 0 → key = HEALTH_ADEQUATE_WITH_TERM Rule 2: healthInsuranceCoverAmount >= 1000000 AND termLifeCoverAmount = 0 → key = HEALTH_ADEQUATE_NO_TERM Rule 3: healthInsuranceCoverAmount > 0 AND healthInsuranceCoverAmount < 1000000 → key = HEALTH_BASIC Rule 4: healthInsuranceCoverAmount = 0 OR healthInsuranceSource = NONE → key = HEALTH_NONE

entry.note: Health covered but no life cover
No health insurance — also triggers Ω medical buffer

table.name: risk_adj_by_health
table.description: Risk adjustment for pre-existing conditions. Conservative default if user declines to share.

table.name: medical_buffer_no_insurance
table.description: One-time medical emergency buffer when user has NO health insurance. Added to Ω.

phase.purpose: Conversational — establish why EF matters before asking for data.
phase.proRole: Handle conversationally. Value-before-ask. Loss framing for myth-busting (factual, not fear). Bridge to ASSESSMENT when user is willing.

phase.purpose: Capture 8 sizing dimensions through adaptive conversation. Deliver value-after insights at cluster boundaries.
phase.proRole: Plan dimension capture sequence, group related dimensions, schedule value-after moments.
phase.keyMechanic: Building Your Picture progress indicator — 8 pills filling with running target estimate.

phase.purpose: Reveal personalised EF target with full attribution.
phase.proRole: Compute final target using formula recipe + mapping tables. Display attribution showing each dimension's impact. Offer D3 social obligation prompt (OPTIONAL). Trigger Starter Shield if applicable.
Compute allocation across three layers based on computed B and employment profile.

phase.purpose: Propose monthly contribution plan with milestone timeline.
phase.proRole: Compute monthly contribution, project milestones, present action steps.

dimension.name: Income Stability
dimension.what: Employment type + employer stability / income pattern
dimension.sizing: Determines H_base via h_base_by_employment mapping table.
dimension.followUps: If salaried → employer type (govt/PSU, large private, startup, mid-size). If business → tenure (3+ years vs newer).

dimension.name: Dependency Load
dimension.what: Who depends on user's income — nature matters, not just count
dimension.sizing: Adjusts M_risk via risk_adj_by_dependency mapping table. Each dependent type adds a specific increment.
dimension.followUps: Aging parents → health insurance status. Children → age bracket.

dimension.name: Insurance Coverage Quality
dimension.what: Health insurance level; term insurance flag
dimension.sizing: Adjusts M_risk via risk_adj_by_insurance mapping table. Also triggers Ω medical buffer if HEALTH_NONE.

dimension.name: Fixed Obligations
dimension.what: Rent/EMI, school fees, premiums — as ₹ or % of income
dimension.sizing: Directly contributes to B (burn rate) via sum of expense fields. High fixed-to-variable ratio signals higher overall risk.

dimension.name: City Tier / Cost of Living
dimension.sizing: Used in Ω medical buffer calculation (medical_buffer_no_insurance table). Also provides context for validating user-reported expenses.

dimension.name: Age Bracket
dimension.sizing: Adjusts M_risk via risk_adj_by_age mapping table.

dimension.name: Household Income Sources
dimension.sizing: Adjusts M_risk via risk_adj_by_income_sources mapping table.

dimension.name: Health Profile
dimension.sizing: Adjusts M_risk via risk_adj_by_health mapping table.
dimension.privacyNote: "Prefer not to say" is always valid → use PREFER_NOT_TO_SAY (conservative default 0.10). Offer text-input fallback. Do not echo verbally.

dimension.name: Open / Contextual
dimension.sizing: Converted to a one-time INR amount added to Ω. Bounded by [0.5 × B, 2 × B]. Pro uses judgment within this bound.
dimension.mechanic: Not a structured question. A 9th BYP pill appears dynamically.
dimension.examples: Supporting brother's education, pending legal case, upcoming major medical procedure

cluster.name: Income Profile
cluster.valueAfter: First range estimate after H_base + income source adjustment. "Based on your income profile, your baseline is roughly X months."
cluster.computeAfter: Pick H_base from h_base_by_employment using employmentType. Pick income source adjustment from risk_adj_by_income_sources. Show preliminary H range: H_base × (1 + income_adj) ± 20%.

cluster.name: Responsibility
cluster.valueAfter: "Safety Net So Far" card showing each factor's impact direction and magnitude.
cluster.computeAfter: Compute dependency adjustment from risk_adj_by_dependency (sum for all dependents). Pick insurance adjustment from risk_adj_by_insurance. Compute B from expense fields. Show updated estimate with attribution.

cluster.name: Context
cluster.valueAfter: Range collapses to final target number.
cluster.computeAfter: Pick age adjustment from risk_adj_by_age. Pick health adjustment from risk_adj_by_health. Pick Ω medical buffer if applicable using medical_buffer_no_insurance. Compute final H_target and EFT.

pattern.description: Categorical inputs (employment type, city, age bracket, yes/no). Auto-proceeds. No tap needed.
Numeric inputs (income, expenses). Confirm chip with ✓ and ✏️. Flow PAUSES until confirmed. Use range pickers/sliders, not blank text fields.
Phase-gate after all 8 dimensions. All data shown as scannable rows. Two CTAs: Looks right / Let me adjust.
User-initiated edit of a prior answer. Recalculates downstream.

scenario.name: Has Existing Savings
scenario.behavior: Assessment in health-check framing. Respect existing effort.

scenario.name: Has Known Target
scenario.behavior: Offer validation, then skip to FUND_ARCHITECTURE with user's number.

scenario.name: Returning Mid-Flow
scenario.behavior: Resume from last step. If more than 30 days, re-verify.

journeyGuardrails.guardrail: Conservative defaults for withheld data. If a dimension is skipped or user declines, use the higher (more conservative) estimate from the mapping table.
D3 social obligation buffer is OPTIONAL. Never mandatory. Surfaced post-target-reveal as add-on step.
Starter Shield fires DETERMINISTICALLY when target ≤ existing savings. This is a backend rule, not a Pro judgment call.
Pro NEVER does arithmetic. All computation is via tool calls (sum, multiply, max, min). Pro picks values from mapping tables and passes them to tools.
For numeric inputs, always use C2_ACTIVE_CONFIRM. Flow pauses until user confirms the number.

variable.name: openContextFactor
variable.note: For D9 — defined dynamically based on what user volunteers

behavioralDesign.principle: EF must be in a separate account/instrument. Friction-by-design for withdrawals.
Show a Starter Shield (₹25K-50K or 1 month) first. Don't show full target upfront to low-income users. Celebrate each tier hit.
Labeled sub-funds: "Medical Shield", "Job Buffer", "Parent Care Fund". Named money is 2-3× less likely to be spent impulsively.
SIP-like auto-debit. Frame as "self-EMI" not savings.
Show the cost of NOT having a fund: credit-card spiral, SIP-stoppage impact.
25%, 50%, "1 Month Protected", "3 Months Secure" — show what user can now survive.

myth.reality: Depends on 8 dimensions. Dangerously low for freelancers/single-income with dependents.
myth.surfaceWhen: At target-reveal — show why their number differs from generic advice.

myth.reality: 36-42% APR. ₹2L emergency becomes ₹3L+ within a year.
myth.surfaceWhen: During assessment if no fund exists.

myth.reality: Selling equity in a crash = crystallizing losses. SIP stoppage destroys compounding.
myth.surfaceWhen: When user mentions MF/stocks as substitute.

myth.reality: Informal safety nets declining with urbanization. Should be a bonus, not a plan.
myth.surfaceWhen: If user indicates joint family support.

myth.claim: I'll start when I earn more
myth.reality: Lifestyle inflation. Start with ₹500/month — the habit matters more than the amount.
myth.surfaceWhen: For low-income/early-career users daunted by the target.

myth.reality: Over-saving in low-yield instruments has opportunity cost. Once funded, redirect to wealth creation.
